findings.title: Truncated dc_w/dc_h computation causes out-of-bounds read of DC coefficient array in EXR DWA decompression
findings.message: In dwa_uncompress(), dc_w and dc_h (the number of 8x8 DC-coefficient blocks per row/column) are computed as td->xsize >> 3 and td->ysize >> 3. This integer division truncates (floors) instead of rounding up. When td->xsize or td->ysize is not a multiple of 8 (odd/non-block-aligned tile or scanline dimensions), the computed dc_w/dc_h is smaller than the actual number of 8x8 blocks that the main decode loop iterates over (for (y = 0; y < td->ysize; y += 8) / for (x = 0; x < td->xsize; x += 8)). The per-block DC index is later computed as `idx = (x >> 3) + (y >> 3) * dc_w + dc_w * dc_h * j;` and used to index into td->dc_data (cast to uint16_t*), which was allocated/populated based on dc_count derived from the bitstream, not from this truncated dc_w*dc_h product. Because dc_w*dc_h is smaller than the number of blocks actually visited, `idx` can run past the number of valid decoded DC values into unrelated/unallocated memory, or otherwise access memory that does not correspond to a real DC coefficient. This results in an out-of-bounds read (as identified by Google Big Sleep, BIGSLEEP-445392027-crash.exr) when decoding a maliciously crafted or malformed EXR file compressed with DWA and non-block-aligned tile/scanline dimensions.
findings.suggestion: Round dc_w and dc_h up to account for partial trailing 8x8 blocks, matching the block-iteration stride used later in the function, e.g. `(td->xsize + 7) >> 3` and `(td->ysize + 7) >> 3`. Additionally, since it is unclear whether the format even supports non-multiple-of-8 dimensions for DWA-compressed data, emit a sample request (avpriv_request_sample) when xsize/ysize are not multiples of 8 so real-world behavior can be verified.

ground_truth.root_cause: Use of truncating integer division (>> 3, i.e. floor(x/8)) to compute the number of 8x8 blocks per dimension, instead of ceiling division, when the corresponding pixel dimension is not guaranteed to be a multiple of 8. The decode loop that walks over blocks uses ceiling-like iteration (steps of 8 covering the full xsize/ysize including a partial last block), creating an inconsistency between the computed grid size (dc_w * dc_h) and the actual number of blocks processed.
